title: ctdose-core: open, auditable CT dose surveillance from DICOM, with a physics reconstruction when the dose attributes are missing
description:
A Python package (MIT) that computes CTDIvol, dose-length product, size-specific dose estimate and effective dose from CT DICOM data. It reads a recorded dose where one exists — from a CT Radiation Dose Structured Report or the image header — and reconstructs one from acquisition physics where none does, which is the common case in public imaging archives. Every value carries its formula, its inputs and its provenance, so a recorded and a reconstructed figure never become interchangeable by accident.

This archive accompanies the manuscript An open-source, provenance-aware framework for reconstructing missing CT dose indices from DICOM metadata. It includes the measured results the manuscript quotes, under results/, together with the scripts that generate them.

No imaging data is redistributed. The surveyed series are identified by Series Instance UID with their per-series licence; the demonstration subject is identified in paper/demonstration_cases.json and retrievable from The Cancer Imaging Archive following docs/REPRODUCING_FIGURES.md; the GPL-3.0 RDSR sample objects remain with their distributor.
